title: Windows fallback for exact Hostinger completed-build log evidence

phases.objective: Execute the canonical GET-only completed-build log reporter on the independent Windows runner pool when the ARM push run has not reached its first durable claim.

e2e_journeys.actor: Repository owner, GitHub Actions Windows runner, and configured Hostinger read credential
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: A squash merge changes only the exact R3C Windows marker on main with the fixed first-line trigger token.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: A secret-free artifact and Incident #4953 result prove whether the exact Production SHA occurs in completed build 019fc51c-3947-7255-aa4d-f55cb8df7658 logs.
steps: Checkout the exact event SHA and verify it remains remote main.
Verify protected Production, one changed marker, exact marker content, and canonical reporter blob identities.
Verify Incident #4953 is open and the R3C binding is unused.
Record a durable claim after all immutable checks.
Run the canonical reporter contract without credential access.
Perform one authenticated GET for exact completed-build logs.
Scrub the configured token from persisted evidence using PowerShell.
Validate the evidence contract and publish the bounded result.
Succeed only when the expected Production SHA is found.
assertions: The runner is windows-latest and exact event SHA is checked out.
The workflow has contents read and issues write only.
No workflow_dispatch, issue_comment, pull-request, or pull_request_target trigger exists.
The provider method is GET only.
No provider mutation, build creation, deployment, release activation, restart, SQL, migration Apply, database mutation, protected-ref mutation, force update, or external business send occurs.
The exact provider token is removed before artifact upload.

phases.objective: Merge inert registration, then merge exactly one marker-only trigger and read the evidence result.
Use an independent runner pool and fail closed on ref, marker, blob, Production, incident, or one-time binding drift.
GET-only evidence performs no provider mutation.
The workflow does not deploy, activate, or restart Production.
